sources.entry: Focus Flow - Complete ecosystem for time management using the Pomodoro technique. MIT Docker/K8S

summary.one_liner: FocusFlow is a self-hostable Pomodoro time-management ecosystem with a Rust backend and a Tauri v2 + SvelteKit desktop/Android client.
summary.what_it_does: The monorepo contains a Rust backend (Axum, Diesel, Tokio) that handles Pomodoro session tracking, a RESTful API documented with OpenAPI/Swagger, WebSocket broadcasting so clients stay in sync, and Web Push reminders via VAPID. The native client app, built with Tauri v2 and SvelteKit, provides a timer UI, task management with categories and priorities, month and week calendar views with task blocks, and a statistics view covering sessions, tasks by priority and category, overdue trends, and peak hours. The app shows system notifications for Pomodoro transitions and reminders. Users enter their backend server URL on first launch. The backend can be run with Docker Compose or Kubernetes manifests in the k8s/ directory.
how_to_run: docker-compose up (backend image ghcr.io/francesco-gaglione/focusflowcloud:latest with a postgres:15-alpine db service)
cd k8s && kubectl apply -f namespace.yaml (then the remaining manifests in the order listed in the README)
cd app && bun install && bun run tauri:dev
notable: Real-time state sync across clients over WebSockets
Clean architecture / domain-driven backend with OpenAPI/Swagger docs
Native apps for macOS, Windows, Linux and Android from Releases
Client asks for server URL on first launch, so no config files are needed in the app
Conventional Commits drive automatic versioning and changelogs
caveats: Full setup details are in an external documentation link that the README points to but does not include
Local development requires Rust 1.77+, Bun, Docker and Tauri prerequisites for your platform
Kubernetes manifests must be applied in a specific order; the README gives no further K8s guidance
